source_text: Nec hoc solum testimonium de eo scripturarum caelestium ueritas perhibet, uerum et per prophetas ante spiritus sanctus aduentum eius in hunc mundum futurum palam mente omnium conscia praedicauit, ne esset obtentus excusationis incredulis uel ignorasse Dei filium Christum uel nescisse futurum saluatoris aduentum, sicut Dauid manifestat dicens: dies diei eructat uerbum et nox nocti indicat scientiam: non sunt sermones nec uerba, quorum non audiantur uoces eorum. in omnem terram exiit sonus eorum et trans fines terrae uerba eorum. in sole posuit tabernaculum suum. id est in manifesto in luce palam se ipsum uenisse monstrauit et praedicationem per prophetas sui ostensione quodammodo omnibus suae praesentiae conprobauit. hoc etiam Esaias, per quem Dominus ipse praesentiam suam clara adnuntiationis manifestatione monstrauit, prophetat et dicit : ipse qui loquebar ueni, id est, qui per prophetas ante aduentus mei futuri praeloquens fueram, is propria nunc atque praeclara uoce praesentiam meam testis mei ipse manifesto. quid euidentius, quid luce praeclarius, quid uerius potest dici ? ut oculis quodammodo perspectus esset uenisse, ipse qui fuerat uenturus, antequam ueniret ostendit, et incredulitate mentes populi perfidi obstruente uenientem nemo cognouit. sicut idem Esaias in prima increpatione populi proclamat dicens: cognouit bos possessorem suum et asinus praesepe domini sui, Israel autem me nesciuit et plebs me non intellexit.
thought_title: The prophets foretold Christ's coming openly
orientation: The author is continuing his argument that the Jewish people have no excuse for unbelief, now citing David and Isaiah as prophets who publicly foretold Christ's coming.
pass_a_gloss: And not only this testimony about him does the truth of the heavenly scriptures present, but also through the prophets beforehand the Holy Spirit publicly foretold his future coming into this world with the mind of all being aware, so that there might not be a pretext of excuse for the unbelieving either that they had not known Christ the Son of God or that they had not known the future coming of the savior, as David makes clear saying: day to day pours forth speech and night to night declares knowledge: there are no speeches nor words of which their voices are not heard. Into all the earth their sound has gone out and beyond the borders of the earth their words. In the sun he placed his tabernacle. That is, in the open, in the light, he showed that he himself had come openly and he confirmed the preaching through the prophets by the showing of himself in a certain way to all of his presence. This also Isaiah, through whom the Lord himself showed his presence by the clear manifestation of announcement, prophesies and says: I myself who was speaking have come, that is, I who before had been speaking beforehand through the prophets about my future coming, I myself now with my own and very clear voice make manifest my presence as my own witness. What can be said more evident, what more brilliant than light, what more true? So that he might be perceived with the eyes in a certain way to have come, he who was going to come showed himself before he came, and with unbelief blocking the minds of the faithless people no one recognized him when he came. As the same Isaiah proclaims in the first rebuke of the people saying: the ox has known its owner and the donkey the manger of its lord, but Israel has not known me and my people has not understood me.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'unbelief' for incredulitas; the adjective here refers to those characterized by unbelief, so 'unbelieving' keeps the root visible.
Literal rendering of the genitive phrase; 'savior' is the standard English for saluator and the brief's argument centers on salvation.

choices.english: day to day pours forth speech
choices.why: Literal word-for-word rendering of the Psalm verse; 'pours forth' captures the vivid verb eructat.
rejected: day to day declares a word

choices.english: In the sun he placed his tabernacle
choices.why: Literal rendering; the author immediately glosses 'in the sun' as 'in the open, in the light,' so the literal image must be preserved.
rejected: He set his tent in the sun
In the sun he pitched his tent

choices.english: with unbelief blocking the minds of the faithless people
choices.why: Uses the glossary terms 'unbelief' and 'faithlessness' (here as adjective 'faithless' for perfidi); the ablative absolute is kept literal.
rejected: since unbelief blocked the minds of the treacherous people
with disbelief obstructing the minds of the perfidious people

choices.why: Literal rendering of the Isaiah citation; 'manger' is the standard English for praesepe.

pass_b_english: Nor is this the only testimony about him that the truth of the heavenly Scriptures presents. Through the prophets the Holy Spirit also foretold openly, before his coming into this world, with the mind of all as witness, so that the unbelieving would have no pretext of excuse—that they had not known Christ the Son of God or had not known that the coming of the savior would take place. David makes this clear when he says: "Day to day pours forth speech, and night to night declares knowledge. There are no words or speeches whose voices are not heard. Their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the earth. In the sun he placed his tabernacle" (Psalms 19:2-5). That is, he showed that he himself had come in the open, in the light, publicly, and by his own showing through the prophets he confirmed the proclamation of his presence to all in some way. Isaiah also prophesies this—through him the Lord himself showed his presence by the clear manifestation of his announcement—and says: "I who was speaking have come" (Isaiah 52:6). That is, I who was speaking beforehand through the prophets about my future coming, now with my own clear voice I myself make my presence known as my own witness. What can be said more evident, more brilliant than light, more true? So that it might be seen with the eyes, as it were, that he had come, he who was going to come showed it before he came, and with unbelief blocking the minds of the faithless people, no one recognized him when he came. As the same Isaiah proclaims in his first rebuke of the people, saying: "The ox knows its owner and the donkey the manger of its lord, but Israel has not known me, and my people has not understood" (Isaiah 1:3).

problems.why: The passage quoted includes verse 5, but the citation stops at 4.
problems.ruling: Source quotes through 'in sole posuit tabernaculum suum' = Psalm 19:5(18:5), but citation says 19:2-4, omitting verse 5.

fixed: The citation should include verse 5, since the quotation continues through 'In the sun he placed his tabernacle' (Psalms 19:5).

last_rejected.why: The Latin phrase is not from Isaiah 52:6; the citation is incorrect.

last_rejected.ruling: Isaiah 52:6 Vulgate reads 'quia ego Dominus loquebar ecce veni'; 'ipse qui loquebar veni' is a close paraphrase, citation correct.
